classification.difficultyReason: Use product-to-sum identities to obtain simultaneous equations and recover both ordered pairs of acute angles.

content.prompt: Find acute angles $\theta$ and $\phi$ for which $$\cos\theta\cos\phi=\frac14\quad\text{and}\quad\sin\theta\sin\phi=\frac14.$$

answer.short:
$(\theta,\phi)=\left(\frac{\pi}{12},\frac{5\pi}{12}\right)$ or $\left(\frac{5\pi}{12},\frac{\pi}{12}\right)$.

Use product-to-sum identities to find $\theta+\phi=\frac\pi2$ and $\theta-\phi=\pm\frac\pi3$.
answer.worked:
The product-to-sum identities give
$$\begin{align*}\cos(\theta-\phi)+\cos(\theta+\phi)&=\frac12\\\cos(\theta-\phi)-\cos(\theta+\phi)&=\frac12.\end{align*}$$
Adding and subtracting these equations gives
$$\begin{align*}\cos(\theta-\phi)&=\frac12\\\cos(\theta+\phi)&=0.\end{align*}$$
Since both angles are acute, $-\frac\pi2<\theta-\phi<\frac\pi2$ and $0<\theta+\phi<\pi$. Hence
$$\begin{align*}\theta-\phi&=\pm\frac\pi3\\\theta+\phi&=\frac\pi2.\end{align*}$$
Solving the simultaneous equations gives
$$\begin{align*}(\theta,\phi)&=\left(\frac\pi{12},\frac{5\pi}{12}\right)\quad\text{or}\quad\left(\frac{5\pi}{12},\frac\pi{12}\right).\end{align*}$$
